articles.title: How to Have Enough: Wendell Berry on Creativity and Love
articles.highlight: “足够是那么浩瀚的甜蜜，我以为它从不曾真正发生，只有可悲的仿制品。”

articles.title: Decoding Decision Correctness from EEG Under High Cognitive Workload in Virtual Reality: Implications for Collaborative Brain-Computer Interface Teams
articles.selectionReason: Open full-text paper; topic brain_computer_interface; quality signal passed; application scenario is clear.

paperCard.problem: 团队决策中，现有聚合方法（如多数投票）只能等成员报告完决定后才能用反应时或信心去调整权重，无法在决定做出前就判断谁的判断更可靠。高工作负荷会降低人的感知可靠性，而人的行为输出未必能完全反映其内心真实状态。
paperCard.method: 让参与者戴上VR头盔完成目标检测任务，同时用脑电帽记录头皮电位。利用决策前的“运动安全窗口”（按键前100毫秒至目标锁定后300毫秒）内脑电信号的空间协方差，经过黎曼几何投影到切线空间，再用逻辑回归分类器区分“这次会正确”还是“这次会错误”。
paperCard.difference: 旧方法主要利用决策后的行为信号（反应时间、口头信心）来修正或解释决策，只能事后补救；该论文尝试在决策窗口内、按键尚未发生前提取“预判正确性”的神经信号，从而使团队能在决策进行中动态加权。
paperCard.innovation: 把黎曼空间协方差脑电特征用于解码“决策正确性”而非“看到的内容”，并验证该信号在高工作负荷下有效、低负荷下无效，说明脑电聚合不是万能的，而是取决于工作负荷条件。
paperCard.implementation: 用VR呈现无人机视角的连续目标检测任务，通过降低照明来造成高负荷。用500Hz的32导脑电记录，离线滤波和ICA去眼电后，取每个试次前按键300毫秒到前100毫秒的窗口，用Ledoit-Wolf收缩估计协方差矩阵，再经黎曼均值投影至切空间，最后用平衡逻辑回归留一被试交叉验证来分类对错。
paperCard.applications: 可用于军事或应急监控团队中，在高负荷任务下辅助组合多名操作员的判断；也可拓展到医疗影像筛查、无人机监视、网络安全告警等需要快速感知决策的多人团队场景。
technicalTerms: BCI：脑机接口，直接用脑电等信号与设备交流。
EEG：脑电图，从头皮记录大脑电活动。
Riemannian geometry：黎曼几何，把脑电协方差矩阵当作一种几何对象，在流形上处理可提高分类稳健性。
Motor-safe window：避开运动执行影响的时间段，确保解码的是决策相关脑活动而不是按键动作。
LOSO cross-validation：留一被试交叉验证，轮流用一个被试做测试来评估泛化能力。
Cognitive workload：认知工作负荷，如任务变难时额外的心理负担。

articles.highlight: 脑电决策可靠性信号并非通用的团队增强工具，而是一种依赖工作负荷的条件性工具。
articles.summary: 该论文研究能否在操作者按键前，从脑电中提前解码其决策是否正确，从而帮助团队在决策形成过程中加权投票。实验发现，在高工作负荷下该脑电解码显著高于随机水平，但在低负荷下因错误样本过少而不可靠。
articles.failureAnalysis: 低工作负荷下行为准确率接近天花板，错误试验太少，分类器几乎无法识别错误决策；高负荷下整体准确率也仅为61.4%，距离实际应用仍有较大距离。
articles.sourceExcerpt: Decoding Decision Correctness from EEG Under High Cognitive Workload in Virtual Reality: Implications for Collaborative Brain-Computer Interface Teams Christopher Baker (corresponding author) c.baker@qub.ac.uk School of Electronics, Electrical Engineering and Computer Science Queen's University Belfast, Belfast, United Kingdom Stephen Hinton s.f.hinton@ljmu.ac.uk School of Psychology Liverpool John Moores University, Liverpool, United Kingdom Tom Reed treed@mail.dstl.gov.uk Defence Science Technology Laboratory, Salisbury, United Kingdom Stephen Fairclough s.fairclough@ljmu.ac.uk School of Psychology Liverpool John Moores University, Liverpool, United Kingdom Virtual reality, Brain-computer interface, EEG decoding, Riemannian geometry, Decision confidence, Cognitive workload, Team decision-making, Pre-emptive signal Abstract Collaborative Brain-Computer Interfaces (cBCIs) offer a promising mechanism to augment team decision-making, but existing approaches rely exclusively on evidence available only after a decision has been made and reported, such as reaction time or stated confidence. This limits their use to explaining or discounting a decision after the fact, rather than informing a team's response before it is finalised. We tested whether spatial-covariance EEG features could instead provide a genuinely pre-emptive signal of an operator's decision correctness, available within the response window itself, and whether such a signal depends on cognitive workload.

en.highlight: The EEG-based decision-reliability signal is not a general-purpose team augmentation tool, but a workload-conditional one.
en.summary: This paper tests whether EEG can predict decision correctness before a team member commits to a response. Using a VR target-detection task, they found above-chance decoding under high workload but not under low workload, suggesting the neural signal is only useful for team weighting under specific conditions.
en.failureAnalysis: Under low workload, behavioral accuracy was near ceiling, leaving too few error trials for the classifier to learn; even under high workload, overall decoding accuracy was only about 61%. The neural signal is not yet robust for practical deployment across all conditions.
en.title: Decoding decision correctness from EEG under high cognitive workload in VR: implications for collaborative brain-computer interface teams

paperCard.problem: Team decision aggregation usually relies on behavioral outputs reported after the decision, missing the opportunity to weight a vote before it is finalized.
paperCard.method: Use EEG spatial covariance features from a motor-safe pre-response window, project them via Riemannian geometry to a tangent space, and train a logistic regression classifier to distinguish correct from incorrect decisions.
paperCard.difference: It moves from post-hoc behavioral weighting (reaction time, confidence) to a pre-emptive neural signal available during the decision window.
paperCard.innovation: It targets decision correctness rather than stimulus category and shows that the neural signal's validity is workload-dependent, guiding when to use collaborative BCI systems.
paperCard.implementation: Collected 500 Hz 32-channel EEG during VR target detection with degraded lighting as workload manipulation. For each trial, used an epoch from 300 ms after reticle onset to 100 ms before response, computed Ledoit-Wolf shrunk covariance, projected to tangent space via Riemannian mean, standardized, and classified with balanced logistic regression under leave-one-subject-out cross-validation.
paperCard.applications: Military or emergency surveillance teams under high workload, medical image screening, drone monitoring, and any settings where rapid perceptual decisions are aggregated across multiple operators.
technicalTerms: BCI: direct communication channel between brain signals and a device.
EEG: recording of brain electrical activity from the scalp.
Riemannian geometry: treating covariance matrices as points on a manifold to obtain robust classification features.
Motor-safe window: time segment avoiding muscle/motor artifacts so the signal reflects decision rather than action.
LOSO cross-validation: training on all but one participant and testing on that held-out participant to assess generalization.
Cognitive workload: mental effort required by the task, e.g., degraded visual conditions.

articles.title: zvec-ai/zvec-grep
articles.selectionReason: AI source passed freshness and evidence-chain gate: GitHub + Community signal
articles.summary: GitHub 页面介绍了一个名为 zvec-grep 的本地优先工作区搜索工具，强调数据留在本地并面向整体工作区进行检索。它同时兼顾人类交互与 AI Agent 调用，定位为 AI 编程或知识工作流中的基础检索件。仓库已有 2807 stars 和近期公开活动，值得关注的是它如何实现安全、低延迟的本地索引与多客户端访问。
articles.failureAnalysis: 失败风险在于它正面竞争成熟的 ripgrep、IDE 内建搜索和 AI 代码助手自带的检索能力；若没有明显更快的索引、更好的语义理解或独特的工作区抽象，用户迁移动力不足。面向 AI Agent 还必须提供稳定的 MCP/API、权限边界和工具调用协议，否则容易沦为演示级项目。本地优先产品通常缺乏云订阅等清晰收费场景，在缺少商业模式的情况下持续维护和生态拓展也会受限。

en.highlight: Local-first search across your workspace, built for humans and AI agents.
en.summary: The GitHub page describes zvec-grep, a local-first search tool for your workspace, emphasizing that data stays on-device while searching across the whole workspace. It targets both human users and AI agents, positioning itself as a foundational retrieval utility for coding and knowledge work. With 2,807 stars and recent public activity, the repo is worth watching for how it delivers fast, private local indexing and multi-client access.
en.failureAnalysis: Key risk: it competes with mature grep/IDE search and built-in AI coding assistance, so it must offer clearly superior local indexing or semantic workspace understanding; serving AI agents also demands a stable MCP/API, permission boundaries, and a credible monetization path.
